findings.title: Recommendation vocabulary contradicts the arch/plan's `review`/`blocked` contract
findings.description: The architecture fixes the new `recommendation` string values as `"review"` (pending-review) and `"blocked"` (review-failed): `{ recommendation: "review", rationale: "Review required before advancing — no review artifact found for slice NNN (type: code).", ... }`, and the slice plan entry explicitly says the branch returns "`review`/`blocked` recommendations." TD-7 instead shows the value of the `recommendation` field as full sentences (`recommendation: 'Review required before advancing'`, `recommendation: 'Blocked: review verdict does not clear threshold'`) and moves the arch's rationale text into the recommendation field. The design is internally inconsistent on this: "Provides to Other Slices" and the Success Criteria refer to "`review` / `blocked` recommendation vocabulary — the stable strings runners route on." Since Amoeba/the arch require "structured `recommendation` values with a stable vocabulary" that runners route on, the actual field value matters. TD-7 must state unambiguously that `recommendation` is exactly `review` / `blocked` (with the sentence text belonging in `rationale`), or the ratified vocabulary is silently broken.

findings.title: Config-read failure mode is not enumerated
findings.description: The gate introduces a new I/O path into the navigator: `resolveGateConfig(this.config)` calls `ConfigManager.get(...)`. `ConfigManager.get` → `readToml` re-throws any non-`ENOENT` error (malformed TOML, permission/encoding error — verified in `packages/core/src/config/ConfigManager.ts:19-27`). The design only covers "no config / `review_enabled` false," which is not the same as a read error. Because TD-3 folds gate evaluation into `deriveSliceStatus()` — whose existing `catch { return base; }` (verified at `packages/core/src/introspection/WorkflowNavigator.ts`) returns a `no-active-slice`/`needs-design` base status — a thrown config error would either propagate out of `getStatus`/`getNext` or be silently swallowed and skip the gate entirely. The latter is a silent pass, violating the arch's "must not silently pass" and "Fail-fast on configuration errors" principles. The design should state the intended handling (e.g., surface a config error rather than defaulting to gating-off).

findings.title: Present-but-unparseable rationale cannot name the parse failure, as the arch requires
findings.description: The architecture requires, for a review file that exists but cannot be parsed: "It is treated as `UNKNOWN` and `review_unknown_as` applies. The rationale returned to the caller names the parse failure explicitly." The design leans the opposite way, deliberately collapsing the distinction: it notes `parseFrontmatter` "never throws — it returns `{ found: false, data: {} }` on any read/parse error… a read failure and a missing frontmatter both surface as 'no `verdict` present.'" With that collapse, the gate cannot distinguish and therefore cannot name the parse failure; TD-7 only requires the rationale to name review type, verdict, and threshold. The "not silently pass" half of the arch requirement is met, but the explicit-rationale half is unreachable under the chosen interface. The design should either restore a parse-failure signal or explicitly record this as a deliberate deviation from the arch.

findings.title: Arch/pre-slice-plan boundary under-specifies which index locates the review artifact
findings.description: For the `slice`, `tasks`, and `code` boundaries the index is the active-slice index, and the design says so. For the `pre-slice-plan`/`arch` boundary there is no active slice, yet the design says only "extend the no-active-slice / pre-slice-plan path for the `arch` gate" and relies on `detectDocuments(projectPath, index, 'arch')`, which requires an index to build the `NNN-review.arch.*.md` prefix (per 240's detector). The source of that index (presumably `extractSliceIndex(project.fileArch)`, the arch's own index, not a slice index) is never stated. Success Criteria require "the correct review type is looked for automatically" at the `arch` boundary and a fixture "for at least the code and arch/slice types," so this index derivation is required to implement and test the boundary. It is inferable from sibling code but is a genuine hidden dependency in an otherwise fully specified design.
findings.location: project-documents/user/slices/241-slice.gate-logic-in-workflownavigator.md#Boundary → signal (how CF knows a phase is done)

findings.title: Case/wording divergence from the arch on `pending-review` vs `review-failed` for UNKNOWN
findings.description: The arch's `pending-review` definition parenthetically allows "verdict is UNKNOWN and `review_unknown_as` treats it as pending," but no `review_unknown_as` value (`fail`/`concerns`/`pass`) maps to "pending," so the clause is vacuous. The design's choice — present-but-UNKNOWN always yields `review-failed` (never `pending`) — is consistent with the arch's own `review-failed` definition ("artifact present, verdict does not clear the threshold") and is the more coherent reading. No change needed; flagging so the arch wording is reconciled in 243 rather than treated as a contradiction later.

findings.title: `score` read/store behavior has no owning slice
findings.description: The architecture states CF "reads `verdict` and (when present) `score`" and that score is "read and stored when present but not enforced in v1." The design excludes only "numeric `score` enforcement (out of v1 per arch)," and neither the 241 plan entry nor any other slice assigns the read/store behavior a home. Since nothing consumes it in v1, this is not blocking, but the named arch behavior is currently unowned and should be either assigned or explicitly declared out of scope.

findings.title: Arch doc still describes v1 as slice-level-only; plan supersedes it
findings.description: The design implements all four boundaries including the `arch`/pre-slice-plan gate, which the arch text still defers ("its gate logic is a later slice within 240; v1 implements only the four slice-level transitions"). The slice plan explicitly supersedes this (slice 244 folded into 241, Phase 4 decision), so the design is correctly aligned with the plan. Recorded so the stale arch statement is reconciled in documentation slice 243.
